verdict: Mixed-to-bull: NVDA new ATH on Morgan Stanley reinstatement; MRVL Investor Day Oct 6 imminent; MU Q4 CEO flags first explicit price-moderation warning — correction-risk thesis crystallizing.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (last 24–72h)

**NVDA new ATH** — NVIDIA hit an intraday all-time high of $237.88 on Oct 2 (+1.34% close). Morgan Stanley reinstated NVDA as its top semiconductor pick. DGX SPARK 64GB system ($4,999) launches Oct 23.

**AVGO +3.35%** — Broadcom rose to $355.14 on Oct 2 on AI revenue acceleration narrative and a fresh Anthropic financing deal.

**MRVL Investor Day Oct 6** — Upcoming; management flagged $18B FY2028 revenue target. Recent custom-silicon wins with Amazon and Microsoft at 18 cloud-provider design-win count. Key catalyst to watch Monday.

**Micron Q4 FY2026 results (≈Oct 1)** — Revenue guided to ~$50B (Q3 was $41.5B, +346% YoY). CEO Sanjay Mehrotra explicitly called out "meaningful moderation in the rate of price increases" for the first time — the first major supplier signal aligned with the baseline correction-risk thesis.

**HIVE/BUZZ** — No news in the last 72h; most recent material event was the Aug 17 $350M 5-year Blackwell Ultra GPU cloud deal. ARR progressing toward $200M year-end target.

## Watchlist Movers
| Name | Move | Catalyst |
|------|------|----------|
| NVDA | +1.34% (Oct 2), new ATH $237.88 | Morgan Stanley top pick reinstatement; DGX SPARK launch Oct 23 |
| AVGO | +3.35% (Oct 2) | AI revenue growth + Anthropic financing narrative |
| MRVL | No move yet | Investor Day Oct 6 — imminent catalyst |
| MU | ~flat post-earnings | Q4 $50B guide but CEO flagged price moderation |

## Context vs Baseline
- **DRAM pricing decelerating sharply**: Q1 +90-95% → Q2 +58-63% → Q3 +13-18% QoQ. HBM prices actually declining even as volumes grow. Tracks the correction-risk baseline.
- **HBM supply surge accelerating**: Micron targeting 100K wafers/month by year-end (up from ~45K), Samsung at 250K/month, SK Hynix shipping 16-layer HBM4 in volume. All three expanding simultaneously — the late-2026 oversupply setup is crystallizing.
- **Hyperscaler capex firm**: $720-745B combined 2026 guidance (Amazon $200B, Google $200B, Meta $135B, Microsoft $115B), up ~77% YoY. No guide-down.
- **Optical**: Coherent doubling InP output ahead of schedule (by end-2026 vs plan). Lumentum blowout August quarter (+15% stock). Stifel raising PTs ahead of fresh earnings. Structural tailwind intact.
- **Solar**: US Section 232 tariff signed Aug 6 — 15% on polysilicon derivatives + MIP ($0.38/W module floor), effective Dec 4. FSLR facing inventory glut but benefits from protected US pricing; imported-input names face cost pressure.

## Signals Flashing
| Signal | Direction | Bull/Bear |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| Conventional DRAM pricing momentum | Decelerating, Q3 +13-18% | Bear (vs Q1 +90%) |
| HBM4 capacity ramp (all 3 suppliers) | Accelerating simultaneously | Bear (2027 oversupply risk) |
| Hyperscaler AI capex | Firm, no guide-down | Bull |
| NVDA stock / sentiment | New ATH, Morgan Stanley top pick | Bull |
| Optical names (COHR, LITE) | Earnings beats, InP ahead of plan | Bull |
| Solar tariff policy | 15% + MIP effective Dec 4 | Mixed (FSLR wins, imports lose) |

## Most Important Development
Micron CEO's explicit acknowledgment of "meaningful moderation in the rate of price increases" on a $50B Q4 guide is the clearest on-record confirmation that the memory pricing supercycle is decelerating — squarely validating the baseline correction-risk thesis. Pair this with all three HBM suppliers simultaneously ramping capacity and the 2027 HBM price correction risk is moving from thesis to near-certainty. Monitor Q4 MU actual results and MRVL Investor Day (Oct 6) closely.
